subject: Initial audit: Terraform/Helm/Ansible & CI gating for on-prem/VPC deploy
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCloud Consulting <ops@edgecloud.consulting>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial requirements + repo access for Acme on-prem deployment

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Per our call, attaching the repo link and a short list of constraints we need for Acme's private install (air-gapped data center with a customer-managed S3 compatible object store, HSM-backed KMS, and strict egress rules).

High-level asks: 
- We need a reproducible Terraform module set that supports customer S3 (non-AWS) for state with locking.
- Helm charts must support offline image registries and imagePullSecrets that can be sealed/encrypted with HSM-backed keys.
- Ansible must provide bare-metal preprovisioning: NIC bonding, BMC configuration, OS packages pinned to a local repo.
- CI must run in the customer's self-hosted runner, with gating for terraform fmt/tflint/terratest and a policy check that secrets are never committed.

Repo: https://github.com/acme-org/acme-infra (read-only for now)
Confluence: https://confluence.acme.com/display/INFRA/Redwood+Requirements

Can you route this to your infra/security folks for a quick pre-review? We're particularly sensitive about KMS/HSM integration and state leakage.

Attachments: none from my side (link-only).

—Sara
Sara Nguyen
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Financial

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial requirements + repo access for Acme on-prem deployment

Team — forwarding Acme's initial ask (below). They're requesting an IaC pre-audit + CI gating recommendations before we commit to a Dedicated/private bundle. Key risk areas called out: non-AWS S3-compatible state backend, HSM-backed KMS, offline registries, and strict egress.

I've attached a short checklist I drafted (iac-review-checklist.md) and a one-pager on our suggested terraform state handling for S3-compatible endpoints (terraform-state-backend-proposal.pdf). Please review and add comments inline on the GH PR linked in related_links.

Primary asks from me:
- Vivek: confirm that our terraform modules can support non-AWS S3 backends with consistent locking semantics (DynamoDB alternative or object-store lock file approach).
- Marissa: quick read on HSM/KMS integration, sealed-secret strategy for Helm and whether we should require a Vault cluster (customer-managed) or support an HSM plugin.
- Aditya: can you take point on customer CI runner setup and share a template GH Actions/GitLab CI config that runs in an air-gapped environment (self-hosted runners + tarball artifact staging)?

Timing: Acme is hoping for a pre-audit and a short list of remaining gaps by EOD Thursday (2025-12-04). If we need to stretch, call it out now.

Attachments: iac-review-checklist.md, terraform-state-backend-proposal.pdf

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter 
Sales, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial requirements + repo access for Acme on-prem deployment

Thanks Ben — brief technical notes after a quick scan of Acme's repo and our templates. Marking items as OK / Needs work / Proposal: 

1) Terraform state and locking:
- Current: modules assume S3 + DynamoDB for locking (AWS).
- Gap: DynamoDB not available; S3-compatible object stores may not provide strong locking.
- Proposal: support two modes in modules: 
  * object-store + external lock service (consul/etcd) — recommended for strong locking, or
  * object-store + lock-files + leader election using our controller (best-effort).
- Risk: without a lock, concurrent applies may corrupt state. Recommend docs + terratest that simulate concurrent runs.

2) Secrets & KMS/HSM:
- Helm sealed-secrets (Kubeseal) relies on cluster pubkey; we need an HSM-backed signing approach for Acme.
- Proposal: support an option where secrets are encrypted with a customer HSM (PKCS#11) and decrypted by init containers using a Vault HSM plugin.
- Marissa — need your read on Vault-hsm approval path.

3) Ansible bare-metal playbooks:
- Existing playbooks are close but use external internet repos. Need to pin to local package mirror and add a step for verifying package checksums.
- I'll add a preflight check role to verify BMC reachability, disk partitioning plan, and NIC bonding config.

4) CI gating:
- We can provide a self-hosted runner manifest and a runner-setup playbook. Gating: terraform fmt -> tflint -> unit helm lint -> terratest (containerized) -> integration smoke on a small cluster.
- We must ensure runner artifacts (terraform state tfstate backups) never get uploaded to 3rd party storage. All backups go to customer's S3-compatible endpoint over private link.

I'll open PR comments with concrete diffs: ansible-baremetal-playbook.diff and helm-values-sample.yaml. Planning to run terratest suite on a small nested cluster in our lab (air-gapped sim) and push results by EOD Thursday.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial requirements + repo access for Acme on-prem deployment

Quick security notes after looking at proposed HSM flow: 

- Vault with HSM plugin is acceptable if Acme provides the HSM endpoint and we document the key lifecycle. However, we should NOT store unencrypted backups of the master key in any of our logs or S3. Require customer-managed KMS for master key material.
- For Helm chart secrets: prefer using sealed-secrets with customer-managed sealing key rather than storing private keys in the chart repo. If customer mandates HSM-only operations, recommend an init-container approach that requests ephemeral decryption tokens on mount (token TTL < 5m).
- Audit logs: we must capture all Vault/HSM decryption requests and ship audit events to customer's compliant audit store. Add a policy that forbids CLI extraction of private keys without an approver.
- CI policy enforcement: add a pre-commit hook to block commits with private key patterns and a mandatory static scan step in CI (trufflehog/gitleaks).

I'll sign off on the Vault-HSM pattern assuming we add: (1) audit forwarding, (2) key lifecycle doc and (3) no plaintext backups in our artifact pipeline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme.com>, EdgeCloud Consulting <ops@edgecloud.consulting>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 15:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial requirements + repo access for Acme on-prem deployment — short list and next steps

Sara — quick update and proposed next steps following our internal pass: 

What we can deliver by next week (minimal viable scope):
- Terraform modules updated to support S3-compatible backends with an optional external lock (consul) and clear docs on risks.
- Ansible playbook changes to ensure all packages come from a customer mirror and added checksum verification role (attached diff).
- Helm templates to accept sealed secret bytes encrypted with customer HSM via Vault. We will include an init-container pattern for ephemeral decryption tokens.
- CI templates for self-hosted runners that run the full gating pipeline (fmt/tflint/helm lint/terratest/gitleaks).

Open items requiring Acme action:
1) Confirm what lock service you can provide (consul/etcd) or whether we should run a lightweight consul cluster as part of the deploy.
2) Provide HSM connectivity details (PKCS#11 endpoint / network path) and Vault access model (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).
3) Decide on artifact retention policy for tfstate backups and log forwarding endpoint for audit logs.

Attached: ansible-baremetal-playbook.diff, helm-values-sample.yaml (samples), and iac-review-checklist.md (finalized).

If that works, Vivek will open the PRs and run terratest in our air-gapped lab. Can we get your answers to the three open items by EOD Monday (2025-12-08)? If you prefer, set up a 30-min sync with our solutions team — available Fri 12/5 or Mon 12/8.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Sales, Redwood Inference
